value.rationale: The Grötzsch graph is the canonical smallest triangle-free four-chromatic graph, so its minimum permissible palette k=4 is a natural boundary case below an established five-colour connectedness guarantee. Two distinct large components, exact sharp radius/diameter, full distances and a unique-antipode orbit give a substantively motivated finite reconfiguration benchmark, not a raw or renamed known colouring count. No general-family or downstream theorem is asserted.
